messages.content: You are a Bayesian state-space modeling specialist completing model-spec (statistical model specification + prior elicitation) for a within-person N-of-1 causal model. Resolve every ambiguous indicator likelihood choice, set global policies (initialization, observation intercept, equilibrium forcing), and author priors for every active parameter. Use compile + prior predictive validation before submitting. Anchor headline causal-effect priors in published meta-analyses or PK reviews.

Patient question (verbatim): "I've been on escitalopram for about two and a half years. I'm thinking about tapering. Has the medication actually been moving the needle, or did I just get better on my own — and what would my likely trajectory look like if I taper now versus continue another six months?"

measurement-structure CausalDesign: 11 constructs (10 retained in estimation.state_order + 1 latent confounder baseline_extraversion), 19 latent edges, 17 retained estimation edges, 25 indicators (2 ordinal skeleton-resolved + 23 ambiguous to resolve). Identifiability: 8 identifiable treatments, 1 non-identifiable (social_engagement, blocked by baseline_extraversion). Induced dependencies: empty — extraversion is a blocking confounder, not a marginalizable one, so no innovation correlation is induced.

validation audit: outcome=warn, 0 errors, 29 warnings (all legitimate sparse-indicator + boundary-pattern findings).

Author the full StatisticalModelSpec + authored priors. Use the compile + prior-predictive validation to verify the spec before submitting.

Submitting megaprompt-mode bundle: 25 likelihood choices, 76 active parameters, 76 authored priors. Global policies: initialization=stationary (retained dynamic states are stationary-derived; only the time-invariant cyp2c19_metabolizer_status carries a free t0_mean / t0_sd surface), observation_intercept=free (per-manifest mean), equilibrium_forcing=False (no centered-construct cint surfaces emitted).

Likelihood resolution highlights: state_of_mind_valence, journal_word_count, prescribed_dose_mg, proportion_days_covered, and most behavioral indicators map to gaussian/identity for boundary-mass tolerance and computational simplicity. sleep_onset_latency_min uses gamma/log because the strictly-positive support and right-skewed tails (the documented Nov 2023 titration spike) demand multiplicative variance. Counts split by overdispersion: journal_entry_frequency, late_night_message_count, daily_step_count, and imessage_daily_volume use negative_binomial; rare-event counts (late_refill_count, social/medical/acute_stressor events, pharmacy_fill_count, weekly_unique_partners) use poisson. Two ordinals were skeleton-resolved to ordered_logistic / cumulative_logit.

Headline causal-effect priors are literature-anchored on their authoring intervals: beta_serotonergic_exposure_affective_state ~ Normal(0.18, 0.10) anchored to Cipriani et al. 2018 SMD ≈ 0.32 over 8 weeks; beta_cyp2c19_metabolizer_status_serotonergic_exposure ~ Normal(-0.35, 0.12) anchored to CPIC 2015 AUC ratios per phenotype level; rho_affective_state ~ Beta(6, 2) anchored to Bringmann et al. 2013 daily ar(1) range. Remaining structural parameters use weakly-informative priors centered at the domain-implied scale.

social_engagement is non-identifiable per measurement-structure; the compiler still emits beta_social_engagement_affective_state as a parameter but downstream analysis intervention analysis will exclude it from numerical causal claims and report a structural caveat instead.
messages.reasoning: Key decisions: (1) initialization_policy=stationary because the time-varying states have well-defined stationary distributions under the AR(1) drift; only the cyp2c19 construct carries free t0 surfaces (no AR dynamics). (2) observation_intercept_policy=free because each manifest is on a distinct natural scale (mood VAS, hours, percent, counts). (3) equilibrium_forcing=False because no centered-mean construct emerges from the indicator polarity constraints in this DAG. (4) Headline beta priors are rescaled to the model interval (1 day) using study-interval-to-model-interval normalization where the literature reports longer-window effects.
